referent_summary: Documented cases of LLM-based systems (paired with evolutionary search or multi-agent tool use) producing new, independently verifiable scientific and mathematical results, plus broader claims that LLMs will autonomously accelerate scientific discovery.
source_of_truth: Google DeepMind (FunSearch, Nature 2023; AlphaEvolve, 2025) and OpenAI (unit-distance conjecture disproof, 2026) technical reports/blog posts
authoritative_statement: DeepMind's FunSearch (Nature, Dec 2023) paired an LLM with an automated evaluator and evolutionary search to find new, verifiable mathematical constructions -- including the largest improvement to the cap-set problem's lower bound in 20 years -- which DeepMind states is the first time an LLM has been used to make a new discovery on an open scientific problem. AlphaEvolve (May 2025), a Gemini-powered evolutionary coding agent, later found a 48-multiplication algorithm for 4x4 complex matrix multiplication, improving on Strassen's 1969 record for the first time in 56 years. Google's multi-agent "AI co-scientist" (Feb 2025) generated a hypothesis about bacterial gene transfer matching an Imperial College London team's unpublished experimental findings. Most recently, an OpenAI general-purpose reasoning model (not specialized for math) autonomously disproved Erdős's 80-year-old planar unit-distance conjecture (May 2026), externally verified by Fields medalist Tim Gowers, who called it "a milestone in AI mathematics" -- OpenAI's strongest framing yet (its own claim: the first prominent open problem central to a subfield of mathematics solved autonomously by AI). Each case is a real, externally verified result; none show an LLM performing open-ended, unprompted, end-to-end science.
evidence_type: direct measurement / controlled demonstration (mathematically or experimentally verifiable outputs)
epistemic_basis: Outputs are independently checkable -- math constructions are proof-verifiable, and the AI co-scientist's hypothesis was corroborated against the researchers' own unpublished wet-lab data -- a stronger evidentiary footing than most AI capability claims, though each case is a narrow, engineered pipeline rather than a general/autonomous LLM discovering things unprompted.
notes: Distinguish these narrow, verified cases (this referent) from the broader, more speculative claim that LLMs will generally/autonomously "do science" end-to-end -- see C041 (Amodei), the head proponent of that broader claim, graded separately as a forecast.

evidence_type: expert judgment / theoretical framework applied to existing systems (not a direct measurement -- consciousness has no agreed empirical test)

referent_summary: Google's disclosure of median Gemini Apps text-prompt energy/water/carbon, published at two measurement boundaries
source_of_truth: Google, 'Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI at Google Scale' (Cloud blog + technical paper arXiv:2508.15734)
authoritative_statement: Median Gemini Apps text prompt (May 2025 data): 0.24 Wh energy, 0.03 gCO2e, 0.26 mL water at the COMPREHENSIVE boundary (active TPU/GPU + host CPU/DRAM + provisioned-idle machines + PUE 1.09 overhead); the SAME disclosure gives 0.10 Wh / 0.12 mL counting active chips only, which Google itself calls 'an optimistic scenario at best' that 'substantially underestimates' the footprint. Median not mean; text prompts only; Gemini Apps only (not API); inference only; median prompt energy fell 33x over the prior 12 months.
epistemic_basis: Operator self-measurement, not independently audited; one source yields two numbers depending on measurement boundary — which number circulates depends on which boundary is quoted.
notes: Component split per the technical paper as reported by MIT Technology Review (https://www.technologyreview.com/2025/08/21/1122288/google-gemini-ai-energy/): accelerators ~58%, host CPU/DRAM ~25%, idle ~10%, overhead ~8%. Critiques: median hides the tail (reasoning/long-context); greenwashing-vs-progress debate (Towards Data Science). Merged 2026-07-05 from provenance register row gemini-energy-per-prompt (primary fetched).

referent_summary: Challenger, Gray & Christmas tallies of US announced job cuts with AI as a company-cited reason
source_of_truth: Challenger, Gray & Christmas monthly Job Cut Announcement Reports
authoritative_statement: 2025: companies cited AI as a reason for 54,836 ANNOUNCED US job-cut plans (~5% of 1,206,374 total announced cuts; 'DOGE Impact' led at 293,753). 2026 YTD-June: 101,743 AI-attributed (~23% of all cuts), AI the leading stated reason for a fourth consecutive month; June 2026 alone 14,029 of 45,849 (31%). Cumulative since AI-reason tracking began (2023): 173,568. Counts are announced cut plans by US-based employers; the reason is coded from company statements — 'company cited AI', not verified causation.
epistemic_basis: Announced != realized (plans get reduced/delayed/achieved by attrition); US-only; reason coding follows company framing and is exposed to AI-washing in both directions; Challenger publishes no formal reason-coding methodology.
notes: 2025 annual: https://www.challengergray.com/blog/2025-year-end-challenger-report-highest-q4-layoffs-since-2008-lowest-ytd-hiring-since-2010/. Skepticism on the record: Altman, Feb 2026 — 'there's some AI washing where people are blaming AI for layoffs that they would otherwise do' (https://fortune.com/article/sam-altman-ai-washing-tech-layoffs/); Oxford Economics (Jan 2026): firms 'don't appear to be replacing workers with AI on a significant scale'; Cognizant CAIO Hodjat: 'sometimes AI becomes the scapegoat'. Secondary coverage circulating '150,000+ AI cuts in H1 2026' conflicts with Challenger's own 101,743 — recorded, not averaged. referent_summary: UNU-INWEH projection of the aggregate 2030 water footprint of AI/data-centre electricity, benchmarked to sub-Saharan Africa's basic water needs
source_of_truth: Aczel, Chamanara, Matin, Farsi, Marwala, Madani (2026), 'Environmental Cost of AI's Energy Use: Carbon, Water and Land Footprints' (UNU-INWEH)
authoritative_statement: Report projects global data-centre electricity rising to ~945 TWh by 2030 (from ~448 TWh in 2025), with an associated water footprint of ~9.3 trillion litres — which the report states 'will equal the basic annual domestic water needs of all 1.3 billion people in Sub-Saharan Africa'. The water footprint combines on-site cooling AND off-site water embedded in electricity generation; the report itself notes the electricity-generation component often exceeds direct facility use and is highly sensitive to energy mix (e.g. shifting from coal to bioenergy could cut carbon ~70% but surge the water footprint ~30x). Inference (not training) is stated to drive ~80-90% of AI energy use.
epistemic_basis: Forward projection to 2030 from compiled primary data; a multi-dimensional footprint model, not a measurement — the water figure is a boundary-dependent aggregate (cooling + electricity-generation water) sensitive to grid/energy-mix assumptions.
notes: Distinct referent from REF-REN-WATER (per-prompt) — this is an aggregate 2030 projection. Lead author Kaveh Madani (2026 Stockholm Water Prize laureate). Report released 3 June 2026; publicized during London Climate Action Week with UN Sec-Gen Guterres calling on AI firms to disclose water/carbon/land impacts (UN AI Environmental Transparency Initiative). The 1.3bn / 9.3-trillion-litre comparison is widely circulated (Time, PBS, UN News, Il Sole 24 Ore, Futurism, FT). Key caveat, from the report itself: most of the 'water footprint' is off-site water embedded in electricity generation, not water data centres directly 'drink' — same boundary subtlety as REF-GOOGLE-GEMINI-FOOTPRINT / REF-REN-WATER. No published third-party rebuttal of the figure found as of 2026-07-08. FT article (source of the tracked circulating variant) not URL-pinned from this harness — verify before quoting.
